solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fruit and nuts, for the most part

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: nuts and bananas are both slang for crazy

explanation.surface: Someone describing a snack mix that is mostly fruit and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bananas means crazy, like nuts; 'for the most part' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a common tropical fruit, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Rob and Mike dividing blame

indicators.note: the letter splits the word for blame into two parts, sitting between them

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two men, Rob and Mike, have someone come between them as a quarrel over blame breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob and Mike look like two names; Rob is a verb, the definition. To ramp is old British slang for to swindle or rob.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a ramp is a swindle, and to ramp someone is to cheat or rob them.

clue.text: Keep calm partner heading towards something

parts.note: a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend
on, as in 'on to', describes moving towards a target

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm as your partner heads off towards something.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is said to someone who is getting overexcited, urging them to calm down.

clue.text: Plant and wider rocks in pool, perhaps

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: pool is an example of a sport, played on a table with cues

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so the letters of wider are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant and rocks set around a pool, perhaps in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like garden stones beside the pool but signals shaking up the letters of 'wider'; pool here is the cue game.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiderwort is a flowering garden plant of the Tradescantia family.

clue.text: Hang around block

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to idle or loiter
second meaning: the head; block is also slang for head

explanation.walkthrough: Loaf for head comes from rhyming slang loaf of bread; block is another slang word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to idle aimlessly, and in British slang a loaf is a person's head, as is a block.

clue.text: Partially exhume rib bones

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to dig up part of a skeleton, a rib among the bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Humeri is the plural of humerus, the long upper-arm bone in the skeleton.

clue.text: Tax lost by country delaying last of fiscal books

indicators.note: putting a letter off till later moves it further along the word

parts.note: Scotland is a country of the UK

indicators.note: picks the final letter of fiscal

parts.note: its final letter is L
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A tax lost to a country because its fiscal books arrived late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' belongs to the definition: scot and lot was a tax that no longer exists, so the setter calls it lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot and lot was a historical English parish tax, long since abolished, hence a lost levy.

clue.text: Yard gatecrashes rank party with hubbub

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers

indicators.note: a gatecrasher gets in uninvited, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An uninvited guest from the yard barges into a smart party amid the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gatecrashes' puts YD between ROWD and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdydow is an informal word for a noisy disturbance or uproar.

clue.text: Behind award for cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the end letter round to the front

parts.note: a BAFTA is a British film and television award

explanation.surface: Someone trailing behind in a race for a cycling prize.
explanation.walkthrough: BAFTA with its last letter moved to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical term meaning towards or at the stern, so behind.

clue.text: Papal ambassador backing revision of Catholic union

parts.note: to be pro something is to back it

indicators.note: a revision reworks the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Vatican envoy supports changes to a Catholic union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' rearranges C plus UNION into NUNCIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronuncio is a papal envoy of nuncio rank serving in a country where he is not the senior diplomat.

clue.text: Extol Anglo-Albanian singer, one succumbing to pressure, making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means read from the end to the start
the one gives way, so it is replaced by pressure

parts.note: Dua Lipa is a British pop singer of Albanian heritage
I is the Roman numeral one
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Praise for a pop star who gave in to pressure and staged a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: In DUALIPA the I gives way to P, making DUALPPA, which 'making a comeback' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to praise or acclaim, just as extolling is praising highly.

clue.text: Finding this newspaper outside shelter, journalist moved rapidly

indicators.note: the paper's letters go round the shelter word

parts.note: the clue appears in the Financial Times, FT
the lee is the sheltered side
ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter finds the paper sheltering outside and hurries off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this newspaper' is the paper the puzzle is printed in, the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleet is an old verb for moving swiftly, so fleeted means sped by.

clue.text: Test case essentially linked to Express

indicators.note: the essence is the heart, so the middle letters

parts.note: its central letters are AS
to express something is to say it

explanation.surface: A test case at its core is tied to a newspaper, the Express.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is an analysis or trial of a substance, such as testing a metal for purity.

clue.text: Run into general absorbed by puzzle about Captain Nemo?

indicators.note: being absorbed means going inside the puzzle's letters
about here means round the other way, so the puzzle word is written in reverse

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle

indicators.note: into puts the run letter inside

parts.note: main means general, as in 'in the main'
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a general who runs into Jules Verne's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into MAIN to make MARIN; REBUS turned 'about' is SUBER, which absorbs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Nemo commands the Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel, so he serves aboard a submarine; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Ireland, e.g. after Reformation, divided on a new basis

indicators.note: a reformation reshapes the letters into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
e.g. without its full stops

explanation.surface: Ireland, after the religious Reformation, was split along new lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R sells the historical Reformation; here it just rearranges IRELAND and EG.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to rearrange groups or boundaries, so realigned describes something split up along fresh lines.

clue.text: Speakers in sideboard included in promotions

indicators.note: the furniture's letters go inside the other word

parts.note: ads are advertisements, which promote things
a dresser is a sideboard with shelves

explanation.surface: Hi-fi speakers built into a sideboard feature in a sales promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Addressers are people who address an audience, so they are talkers or orators.

clue.text: Apparel taken by old foe unexpectedly depressed Puck

parts.note: robing is clothing, robes

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters come out in a surprising order

parts.note: taken as written
low means depressed

explanation.surface: An enemy unexpectedly seizes clothing and Puck is downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is the folk name of the mischievous sprite Puck in English folklore and Shakespeare.

clue.text: Startles, pressing hooter such as crew might use?

indicators.note: the outer word presses round the bird

parts.note: rocks means shocks or startles
an owl hoots

explanation.surface: A sudden blast on a horn startles a boat crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' looks like a horn but is the bird. Crew is rowing, as in a boat race.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowlocks are the fittings on a boat's side that hold the oars, which rowers need.

clue.text: Electrician extremely reluctant to break cover of cassette deck

indicators.note: extreme letters are the first and last

parts.note: its ends are E and N

indicators.note: the word for reluctant breaks into the cover letters
the cover is the outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: its ends are C and E
loth means unwilling

explanation.surface: An electrician unwilling to remove the casing of a cassette deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like the cassette player but is the verb, to adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone out is to dress or adorn them, and enclothe means to clothe.

clue.text: Chicken today went badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A report that things went badly for a chicken today.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wyandotte is an American breed of domestic fowl.

clue.text: Loose excrement picked up in flat

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the other

parts.note: flat, of a speech or wine, means dry

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means read upwards

parts.note: poo is excrement

explanation.surface: Someone cleaning up dog mess in their apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like the home but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy means sagging, hanging limply, as something loose does.

clue.text: Shiatsu techniques holding back stellar group

indicators.note: back means read from right to left
the phrase holds the letters within it

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Massage techniques that work on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Cetus, the whale, is a constellation, a group of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Leaves seaport north of Sweden

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Split is a seaport in Croatia
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone departs from a port up north of Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: Splits is a verb, meaning goes away or departs, informal for leaves.

clue.text: Inauspicious and ordinary, diminished by stifling love

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the outer word holds the inner letter

parts.note: minus means reduced by
love is zero, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: Ordinary life diminished by stifled love sounds an unlucky sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means threatening or full of bad omens, the same as unpromising or inauspicious.

clue.text: Agile agent crossing river

indicators.note: the agent's letters span the river letter

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A nimble secret agent fording a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and nimble, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Second onlooker losing specs when changing in Tube?

indicators.note: changing means the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
OO looks like a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: A bystander loses their glasses while changing trains on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' suggests the London Underground; it is a breathing tube. 'losing' takes two O's from ONLOOKER before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel is a breathing tube used by swimmers just below the water's surface.

clue.text: Terms of special licence overseen by state channel

indicators.note: in a down clue being overseen means coming below

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky, a US state

indicators.note: terms are ends, here the last letter of each word

parts.note: its final letter is L
its final letter is E

explanation.surface: Terms of a special broadcasting licence supervised by a state TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' looks like TV but is a strait.
explanation.definitionFit: A kyle is a Scottish name for a narrow strait or sound, a sea channel.

clue.text: Conductor's back to work line before broadcast of Mikado?

indicators.note: the back is the end, so the last letter

parts.note: its final letter is K

indicators.note: broadcast signals the word as it is heard aloud

parts.note: the Mikado is the emperor of Japan

explanation.surface: A conductor goes back to work on a broadcast of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto Klemperer was a German conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Klemperer was a famous twentieth-century orchestral conductor, known for Beethoven and Mahler.

clue.text: Composer left mobbed by crowd

indicators.note: being mobbed means surrounded, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a host is a great crowd

explanation.surface: A composer is surrounded by fans after he leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets suite.
